findings.issue: "payloadPath": "line_item_groups" — this field does not exist on the orders/paid webhook payload. Shopify's order payload exposes a `line_items` array with per-line properties; there is no top-level `line_item_groups` field. The coding agent will read undefined on every paid order, so the `increment-bundle-purchase-count` capability will never correctly identify which bundles were purchased, silently producing zero increments for all orders.
findings.fix: Remove the "order line item group ids" signalField and its binding entirely; instead, identify bundle purchases by matching `line_items[].variant_id` (already bound) against the `bundle_components` table, or by reading a bundle-id cart line attribute stored as a line item property at add-to-cart time (source="resolved", resolution="read _bundle_id from line_items[].properties where name='_bundle_id'").

findings.issue: "the products/delete webhook carries only the product id; mark all bundle_components referencing that product external id as deleted" — the plan declares NO trigger for `products/delete`. Only `products/update` is wired as a trigger. A deleted product never fires `products/update`, so this edge case describes behavior the system has no mechanism to execute; deleted-product components will remain marked "available" in `bundle_components` indefinitely.
findings.fix: Add a second external-event trigger for the event "a product is deleted", bound to shopifyTopic `products/delete`, with signalField "product external id" → payloadPath "id", and an idempotency rule of unconditional overwrite keyed by product external id.

findings.issue: "op": "product" — this is a single-resource lookup by ID, but the capability's dataNeeds include "search query text" and "pagination cursor", and its description says "search and retrieve products". A single-product-by-ID query cannot satisfy a free-text search with pagination; the op resolves the wrong operation and the coding agent will implement a non-functional product search.
findings.fix: Replace the shopifyStep op with the products list/search operation (e.g. `products` query with a `query` argument for text search and `after` cursor for pagination), and update produces/consumes accordingly.

findings.issue: "op": "discountAutomaticBasicUpdate" — this step is applied unconditionally for all bundle updates, but BXGY bundles require `discountAutomaticBxgyUpdate`. Calling `discountAutomaticBasicUpdate` on a BXGY discount node will either return a Shopify API error or silently mutate the wrong fields, corrupting the discount configuration for any merchant who edits a BXGY bundle.
findings.fix: Branch the second shopifyStep by discount kind: use `discountAutomaticBasicUpdate` for percentage/flat bundles and `discountAutomaticBxgyUpdate` for BXGY bundles; document this conditional in the step's `consumes` field so the coding agent applies the correct mutation.

findings.issue: Both `discountAutomaticActivate` and `discountAutomaticDeactivate` are listed as sequential shopifySteps (step 1 then step 2). The coding agent will read this as a two-step protocol and call both ops on every toggle invocation — activating and then immediately deactivating (or vice versa) — leaving the discount in the wrong terminal state every time.
findings.fix: Declare only one conditional step: call `discountAutomaticActivate` when desired enabled state is true, or `discountAutomaticDeactivate` when false; document this branching in the step's `consumes` field rather than listing both ops as a sequence.
